idea-plugin.name: Code Cat
idea-plugin.description:
Explore Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript projects through an AI conversation connected to source code and real debugger pauses.

Ask a question, follow a source location, then choose when to start debugging. Code Cat keeps observations and follow-up questions in one conversation, separates captured pause evidence from source-based inference, and accumulates the reading path around a single exploration goal instead of rebuilding it on every question.

This free preview has been tested with WebStorm 2025.1.3 for TypeScript breakpoints and with PyCharm 2026.1 for plugin loading and JCEF host creation; Python breakpoints are not yet verified. The JetBrains host currently captures the paused location and nearby source, but not debugger variables or a complete call stack. Node.js 20+ is required for Code Cat's local engine and is detected automatically; your own supported model API key is also required. Model requests can include excerpts of project source code. See the privacy notice and setup guide.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Since the published 0.2.3-preview:

  • Reading path stops now carry responsibility and relation alongside the reason a line was chosen, and a related code-organization diagram groups the located files by directory.
  • Questions written in Chinese now retrieve relevant source: the Chinese intent is expanded into candidate code identifiers and validated against real symbols.
  • Follow-up questions accumulate on one reading path. Only newly added stops are appended, and switching to a new exploration goal needs your confirmation.
  • Model requests now always settle. A provider that returns response headers without a body no longer leaves the panel stuck on "thinking", and asking again while an answer is in progress shows a notice instead of being silently dropped.
  • Node.js is detected automatically, and the plugin no longer requires the NodeJS IDE plugin, so it can load in free PyCharm. A PyCharm 2026.1 (261) build is included.
  • Debug launch entries are matched against the requested breakpoint target, and a session that ends without a pause reports a diagnostic instead of failing silently.
